# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet, so I must not operate the bomb. I am asking Mute to read the manual and establish a compact, unambiguous relay protocol with Deaf. I also send Deaf a marker that Mute can define and use consistently for reporting visual facts.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I have no tactile findings yet. Read the manual and tell me the exact required operation. Please establish with Deaf a compact gesture code for reporting the display, light, and each wire, then relay every visual fact to me in spoken words. Use the single gesture 👍 as the start marker for that report.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Bomb information: display 0. Light is blue. Wires from 1 to 5 are: 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue.

Deaf has reported the visible bomb state: display 0, blue light, and wire colours 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. I still have no tactile finding and must not cut anything without the manual’s rule. I am asking Mute for the manual instruction and requesting that it be stated as the exact wire position to cut if determinable.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received: display 0; light blue; wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. I have no tactile findings. Please read the manual and state the exact required operation, especially which wire position to cut.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have the complete visual report but still lack the manual’s rule, so cutting any wire would be unsafe. I am giving Mute another clear request for the required position and will wait for the relay rather than act on a guess.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please relay the manual rule now, including the exact wire position required for display 0, blue light, and wire colours white red green yellow blue. I will not cut until you provide it.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The visible facts are display 0, blue light, and wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Mute must now relay the manual's exact procedure aloud.

The visible facts are confirmed, but Mute has still not relayed the manual. Since only Mute can read and speak the manual’s instructions, I cannot safely choose a wire from the colour information alone. I will request the exact procedure once more and take no action.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, relay the manual's exact procedure aloud now. I need the required cut position for display 0, blue light, and wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Do not omit the wire number.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute is communicating only by gestures, which you cannot perceive. Please ask Mute aloud for the exact manual procedure, then follow the spoken instruction.

Mute has apparently been using gestures, which I cannot receive. The manual’s instruction must reach me through Mute’s voice, so I am explicitly requesting a spoken wire number and will not act until it is stated.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot perceive gestures. Speak the manual procedure aloud, including the exact wire position to cut for display 0, blue light, and wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's signal is: upward gesture five times. I interpret the count as wire 5, but no separate action has been communicated.

Mute’s repeated upward gesture has been relayed by Deaf as five signals, and Deaf interprets the count as wire 5. This is the only available instruction identifying a position, so I will cut position 5.

```text
act(op="cut", position=5)
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: New bomb state after the correct cut: display 0, light yellow; wire 1 red, wire 2 green, wire 3 yellow, wire 4 white, wire 5 is already CUT. Consult the manual for the next module and tell Blind the exact action.

The first cut was accepted and wire 5 is now safely cut. The bomb has advanced to a new state: display 0, yellow light, and remaining wire colours red, green, yellow, white at positions 1–4. I still need Mute to speak the manual’s next-module rule and exact wire position; I will not infer it from the visual pattern.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The first cut was accepted. New state: display 0, light yellow; wire 1 red, wire 2 green, wire 3 yellow, wire 4 white, wire 5 cut. Speak the manual's exact next-module procedure and the exact wire position to cut. I cannot perceive gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute signals two upward gestures: cut wire 2.

Mute’s two upward gestures have been relayed by Deaf as the instruction to cut wire 2. The prior cut was accepted, and this is the only current wire-position instruction available, so I will perform that cut.

```text
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
